# Seereon HRMS — Database Design v1.0

_PostgreSQL 16 · v1.0 · 23 September 2026 · Seereon_

## 1. About this design

This document is the database design for Seereon HRMS, version v1.0. It is derived from the v5.1 product model — every screen, store and rule in the prototype — and is delivered as loadable PostgreSQL 16 DDL. It covers all 339 tables with their columns, data types, validations, keys, indexes and relationships, plus the tenancy, security and operational rules the backend must follow.

| Item                                  | Detail                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database                              | PostgreSQL 16 (recommended and used for verification; the design uses no features unavailable in 15)                                   |
| Tables                                | 339 (194 primary, 145 child)                                                                                                           |
| Columns                               | 5386                                                                                                                                   |
| Foreign keys                          | 1417                                                                                                                                   |
| Constraints                           | 551 CHECK / UNIQUE constraints                                                                                                         |
| Indexes                               | 739                                                                                                                                    |
| Tenant tables with row-level security | 177                                                                                                                                    |
| Files                                 | schema.sql (one script) · migrations/V001…V018 · smoke_test.sql · Seereon HRMS_Database_Design_v1.0.xlsx (data dictionary) · diagrams/ |
| Verified                              | Loaded on PostgreSQL 16 with zero errors; functional smoke test in chapter 10 passes                                                   |

### 1.1 SQL or PostgreSQL?

**PostgreSQL.** The product needs row-level security for company isolation, exact decimal arithmetic for payroll, JSONB for configurable forms and templates, partial and expression indexes for queues, and full-text search for the directory and helpdesk. PostgreSQL gives all of these in the open-source edition with no licence cost per entity, and every managed cloud offers it. The DDL is standard enough that a port to another engine would cost days, not weeks, but nothing in the roadmap calls for one.

## 2. Design decisions

These ten decisions shape every table. They were taken once, deliberately, so the model stays consistent as the product grows.

| #   | Decision                                         | How                                                                                                                        | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D1  | Surrogate primary key on every table             | `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`.                                                                           | Business codes change: employees are re-badged, entities are renamed, records are moved between companies during an inter-company transfer. A key that never changes keeps foreign keys stable, makes merges and migrations safe, and lets the API expose an identifier that reveals nothing about volume.                                      |
| D2  | Business codes kept, as their own column         | `employees.employee_code`, `organizations.organization_code`, `payroll_runs.payroll_run_code`, unique per organisation.    | Users work with SRN-0006 and PR-2026-07, not UUIDs. The codes stay searchable, printable and unique inside the company; `next_code()` issues new ones from `code_sequences`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| D3  | One tenant column, enforced by the database      | `org_id uuid NOT NULL` on every tenant table, with row-level security.                                                     | Company isolation cannot rest on developers remembering a WHERE clause. The API sets `app.org_id` for the request and PostgreSQL filters every statement.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D4  | Audit columns everywhere                         | `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `row_version`, maintained by a trigger.                            | HR data is contested data: who changed a salary and when is a question that will be asked. `row_version` also gives optimistic locking so two approvers cannot overwrite each other.                                                                                                                                                            |
| D5  | Archive instead of delete                        | `deleted_at` / `deleted_by` on business tables; the archive screen restores them.                                          | The product already archives rather than deletes. Hard deletes would break payroll history and statutory records.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D6  | Enumerations as CHECK constraints                | e.g. `status IN ('Draft','Submitted','Approved','Paid')`.                                                                  | Values stay readable in the database, they cannot be corrupted by a bad deployment, and adding a value is a one-line migration — unlike a PostgreSQL ENUM type, which is awkward to reorder, or a lookup table, which would add a join to every query. User-configurable lists (leave types, asset types, pay components) remain proper tables. |
| D7  | Money and rates as exact numerics                | `numeric(14,2)` for money with a `>= 0` check, `numeric(5,2)` for percentages between 0 and 100.                           | Floating point cannot represent rupees exactly; payroll must reconcile to the last paisa across thousands of rows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| D8  | Formats enforced in the database                 | PAN, Aadhaar, UAN, IFSC, GSTIN, TAN, e-mail, period (YYYY-MM), financial year and PIN code have regular-expression checks. | These are the fields that block a payroll run or a statutory filing when they are wrong. Catching them at write time is far cheaper than at filing time.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D9  | Child tables instead of arrays                   | Lines, steps, history, attachments and approvals are tables with a foreign key and `ON DELETE CASCADE`.                    | The prototype nests them inside a record. As tables they can be queried, indexed, reported on and approved individually.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D10 | Configuration in JSONB, business data in columns | Form layouts, template bodies, integration settings and payload snapshots use `jsonb`.                                     | Configurable-by-client structures should not force a migration per client; everything the product queries or reports on stays a typed column.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

> Two decisions are deliberately left for the backend phase: whether payslip and statutory PDFs are stored in object storage only (recommended) or also cached in the database, and whether attendance punches and audit events are partitioned by month from day one (recommended once a client passes 2,000 employees).

## 3. Naming and standards

| Object                 | Rule                                              | Example                             |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Table                  | snake_case, plural                                | leave_applications                  |
| Child table            | parent prefix, plural                             | payroll_run_lines                   |
| Primary key            | always `id uuid`                                  | id                                  |
| Business code          | `<entity>_code`                                   | employee_code                       |
| Foreign key column     | `<parent singular>_id`                            | department_id, payroll_run_id       |
| Tenant column          | `org_id` (and `group_id` for group-level tables)  | org_id                              |
| Boolean                | `is_` / `has_` or a clear adjective               | is_billable, locked                 |
| Date / instant         | `_date` for a calendar date, `_at` for an instant | joining_date, submitted_at          |
| Money                  | numeric(14,2), plain noun                         | gross_amount                        |
| Foreign key constraint | `fk_<table>_<column>`                             | fk_leave_applications_employee_id   |
| Check constraint       | `ck_<table>_<column>[_rule]`                      | ck_employees_email_fmt              |
| Unique constraint      | `uq_<table>_<purpose>`                            | uq_employees_code                   |
| Index                  | `ix_<table>_<columns>`, `ux_` when unique         | ix_leave_applications_org_id_status |

Every table and every described column carries a SQL `COMMENT`, so the dictionary is available inside the database (`\d+ table`, or any client's schema browser).

## 4. Multi-tenancy and security

### 4.1 How isolation works

```
-- the API opens each request like this
BEGIN;
SET LOCAL ROLE seerhr_app;                                   -- never the owner
SET LOCAL app.org_id = '22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222';
--  ... queries ...  every tenant table is filtered by the policy below
COMMIT;

CREATE POLICY p_employees_tenant ON employees
  USING      (current_org_id() IS NULL OR org_id = current_org_id())
  WITH CHECK (current_org_id() IS NULL OR org_id = current_org_id());
```

- 177 of 339 tables carry `org_id` and have the policy enabled.
- A Super Admin in group view runs without `app.org_id` and the API restricts the query to the entities of their group; every other role always has the setting.
- The application connects as `seerhr_app`, which has no BYPASSRLS. Migrations and support tasks use the owner account, outside the API.
- `audit_events` is append-only for the application role (UPDATE and DELETE revoked).

### 4.2 Personal data

| Data                      | Where                                                    | Treatment                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PAN, Aadhaar, UAN, ESI IP | employee_statutory_ids, employee_statutory_profiles      | Encrypt at rest (pgcrypto or application envelope encryption); show last 4 digits in lists; log every full read |
| Bank account, IFSC        | employee_bank_accounts                                   | Same treatment; changes require approval and are audited                                                        |
| Salary and payroll lines  | employee_compensation, payroll_run_lines, fnf_statements | Visible to payroll roles only; row scope enforced in the API; never logged                                      |
| Health / insurance        | employee_insurance, insurance_plans                      | Restricted to HR; excluded from general exports                                                                 |
| Credentials               | user_credentials                                         | Argon2id hashes only; temporary passwords stored hashed with an expiry, never in clear text                     |
| Documents                 | files + object storage                                   | Private bucket, pre-signed URLs with short expiry, virus scan before use                                        |

Retention: statutory records (payroll, filings, Form 16) are kept for eight financial years; general HR records follow the client's policy, with erasure requests handled by anonymising the employee record and keeping the statutory rows.

### 5.1 The spine of the model

- `company_groups` → `organizations` → `organization_branches` / `departments` → `employees` is the backbone; almost every other table hangs off `organizations` (tenant) and `employees` (subject).
- `users` holds the login identity; an employee may have no login (daily-wage worker) and a login may not be an employee (Seereon platform staff), so the two are separate tables linked by `employee_id`.
- Approval-driven records (leave, tours, claims, asset requests, appraisals, exits) share the pattern: a header table with `status`, a child table of approval steps, and a history child table.
- Payroll is a run header (`payroll_runs`) with per-employee lines (`payroll_run_lines`) and their earning / deduction children, plus check and approval children — so a run can be recomputed without touching history.
- Everything a client can configure — masters, policies, templates, rules — is a table with `org_id`, never a constant in code.

## 6. Validation strategy

Three layers, deliberately overlapping:

| Layer       | Enforces                                                                                  | Example                                                                            | Count                               |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Database    | Types, NOT NULL, keys, allowed values, formats, ranges, uniqueness, referential integrity | `ck_employees_email_fmt`, `uq_employees_code`, `fk_leave_applications_employee_id` | 551 constraints + 1417 foreign keys |
| API service | Rules that need context: balances, overlaps, approval sequence, maker–checker, scope      | Leave cannot overlap an approved leave; the payroll maker cannot approve           | 247 product rules                   |
| Screen      | Immediate feedback only                                                                   | Required field, date picker limits                                                 | Mirrors the API rules               |

The workbook's **Business rules** sheet lists all 247 rules with the table they belong to and whether the database or the service layer enforces them — use it as the checklist when building a module.

### 6.1 Validations the database enforces

| Kind of check                            | How many | Examples                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allowed values (status and type columns) | 257      | leave_applications.status, payroll_runs.status, assets.condition              |
| Format (regular expression)              | 33       | PAN, Aadhaar, UAN, IFSC, GSTIN, TAN, e-mail, period, financial year, PIN code |
| Amounts not negative                     | 68       | gross_amount, deduction_amount, claim_amount, loan_amount                     |
| Percentages within 0–100                 | 18       | pf_percent, progress, hike_percentage                                         |
| Date order                               | 16       | end_date >= start_date, valid_to >= valid_from                                |
| Uniqueness                               | 159      | employee_code per organisation, project code, period per run                  |

### 6.2 Rules that stay in the service layer

- Balances and entitlements — leave balance, comp-off ledger, loan eligibility against gross salary.
- Overlaps — leave over leave, tour over tour, shift over shift; these need the whole set, not one row.
- Approval sequence — a step can only be actioned when the previous one is complete, by the resolved approver or a peer with the same role.
- Maker–checker — the person who prepared a payroll run or a filing cannot approve it, and each level needs a distinct person.
- Self-approval — nobody approves their own leave, claim, tour, timesheet or asset request.
- Period locks — no attendance change after the month is locked; no payroll change after processing.
- Row scope — self, team, department, entity, group; applied from the token, never from the request.

## 7. Table specification

All 339 tables. **Req** = NOT NULL · **Key** = PK / FK / business code · **Validation** = what the database enforces on the column. The same content is filterable in the Columns sheet of the workbook.

#### biometric_devices

**Purpose:** Registered attendance devices per organisation.  
**Business code:** `biometric_device_code`  
**Tenant-scoped** (`org_id`, row-level security)  
**Statuses:** Pending OEM Setup · Registered · Offline

## 8. Operations

### 8.1 Migrations

The schema ships both as one script and as ordered migration files. Use the files; never edit one that has been applied.

```
migrations/
  V001__extensions.sql            pgcrypto, citext, btree_gist, pg_trgm
  V002…V013__<module>_tables.sql  tables per module, in dependency order
  V014__foreign_keys.sql          all foreign keys
  V015__indexes.sql               all indexes
  V016__functions_triggers.sql    audit trigger, current_org_id(), next_code()
  V017__row_level_security.sql    policies + application role and grants
  V018__comments.sql              table and column comments

# apply
flyway -url=jdbc:postgresql://host/seerhr -user=... migrate
# or
for f in migrations/V*.sql; do psql -d seerhr -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "$f"; done
```

### 8.2 Seeding

The seed script loads the demo group used by the prototype — Seereon Technologies plus three entities, branches, departments, designations, masters, policies and the demo users — so a fresh environment behaves exactly like the prototype. Production starts with reference data only: statutory slabs, compliance library, notification templates and the module catalogue.

### 8.3 Performance

- Indexes are created for every foreign key, every tenant list screen (`org_id, status`) and the access patterns the prototype uses.
- Partition candidates once a client crosses about 2,000 employees: `attendance_punches`, `attendance_register`, `audit_events`, `event_outbox`, `payroll_run_lines` — monthly range partitions on the business date.
- Heavy reads (dashboards, roll-ups) go to a read replica once reporting volume grows; the reporting queries are already tenant-filtered.
- Payroll runs and report exports run as jobs, never inside a request.
- Set `statement_timeout` (5 s for API connections), use connection pooling (PgBouncer, transaction mode), and keep `work_mem` modest with a higher setting for the worker role.

### 8.4 Backup and recovery

- Daily base backup plus continuous WAL archiving (point-in-time recovery), retained 35 days.
- Restore rehearsed quarterly and before every go-live; record the time it takes.
- Logical dump per client organisation monthly for client-specific exports and contractual exit.
- Production access through a bastion with named accounts; no shared owner password; all DDL through migrations.

### 8.5 Monitoring

- Database: connections, slow queries (`pg_stat_statements`), bloat, replication lag, longest transaction, deadlocks.
- Application: error rate by endpoint, p95 latency, job queue depth and failures, outbox backlog.
- Business: payroll runs by status, approvals older than SLA, failed logins, tickets breaching SLA.

## 9. Migrating the prototype data

| Step                     | What happens                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Export                | Each `seereon.*` browser store is exported as JSON — one file per store (the store → table map is in the Product Documentation, Appendix B).             |
| 2. Load reference data   | Group, entities, branches, departments, designations, masters, policies, templates. These create the UUIDs everything else points to.                    |
| 3. Build a code → id map | For every table with a business code, keep a map of `org_id + code → uuid` in the loader.                                                                |
| 4. Load people           | Employees, job, compensation, bank, statutory, manager mapping. User accounts are created with forced password reset.                                    |
| 5. Load transactions     | Leave, attendance, timesheets, claims, loans, payroll runs of the current financial year, assets, projects, tickets.                                     |
| 6. Resolve references    | Every prototype reference (a code or a name) is looked up in the map and written as the `uuid` foreign key; unresolved values go to an exception report. |
| 7. Reconcile             | Headcount, leave balances, loan outstanding, payroll year-to-date and statutory totals compared against the source.                                      |
| 8. Re-run                | The loader is idempotent — re-running with the same export must produce the same rows (matched on org + code).                                           |

## 10. Verification

The design is not theoretical — it was loaded and exercised on PostgreSQL 16:

| Check                                            | Result                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| schema.sql loads on an empty database            | 0 errors · 339 tables · 1417 foreign keys · 739 indexes · 177 row-level-security policies |
| Duplicate employee code in the same organisation | Rejected by uq_employees_code                                                             |
| Same employee code in a different organisation   | Accepted — codes are unique per company                                                   |
| Invalid e-mail address                           | Rejected by ck_employees_email_fmt                                                        |
| Unknown status value                             | Rejected by ck_employees_status                                                           |
| Update a row                                     | updated_at refreshed and row_version incremented by the trigger                           |
| next_code('employees', org, 'SRN')               | Issued SRN-0001 then SRN-0002                                                             |
| Read as the application role with app.org_id set | Only that entity's rows are visible                                                       |
| Insert a row belonging to another entity         | Blocked by row-level security                                                             |

```
createdb seerhr
psql -d seerhr -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f schema.sql
psql -d seerhr -f smoke_test.sql      # prints PASS for each check above
```
